title: Cas A (NIRCam image)
caption: The supernova remnant Cassiopeia A, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: Cas A · constellation Cassiopeia · about 11090 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, D. Milisavljevic (Purdue University), T. Temim (Princeton University), I. De Looze (University of Gent)

recognition.text: Ranked #86 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A roughly circular cloud of gas and dust fills the frame. Its inner shell is built from bright pink and orange filaments, dotted with knots that resemble fragments of broken glass, and wrapped in curtains of wispy material like smoke from a campfire. This is Cassiopeia A, or Cas A, the remains of a star that exploded, imaged in high definition by Webb's NIRCam.

Those pink and orange knots contain sulfur, oxygen, argon and neon that came from the star itself. Only NIRCam's fine resolution can pick them out, and they hint at how the star shattered like glass in the explosion.

The smoky outskirts show where material blasted out by the explosion is slamming into gas the star shed before it died. Researchers conclude that this white glow is synchrotron radiation, made by very fast charged particles spiralling around magnetic field lines.
scale: The source lists a distance of 11090 light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 11,000 years ago.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam. The caption explains that the pink and orange knots are gas from the star and the white glow is synchrotron radiation, but the full filter-to-color mapping is not published by the source.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, so the colors here translate wavelengths we cannot see.

explore: Several light echoes also appear, most clearly in the bottom right corner. There, light from the long-ago explosion has reached distant dust and warmed it, and the dust glows as it cools. Clumps of dust outside the nebula are colored yellow, and stars show as blue and white points.
alt: A roughly circular supernova remnant with a bright pink and orange inner shell of knotted filaments, wrapped in smoky wisps, with yellow dust clumps outside and blue and white stars.
